name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,613

clue.text: Surprisingly mobile blood clots

indicators.note: something that happens surprisingly comes out in an unexpected form, so the letters land in an unexpected order

blocks.note: taken as written, all six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A medical warning that clots in the blood can unexpectedly travel around the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile blood clots' reads as one phrase, and a travelling clot really is what EMBOLI are, but 'mobile' is only the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Emboli is the plural of embolus, a clot or other mass that lodges in and blocks a blood vessel.

clue.text: Remove hair from pie cooked near the end of the night

indicators.note: cooked ingredients are transformed, and cooked books are falsified, so the letters are changed around

blocks.note: taken as written

blocks.clueFragment: near the end of the night
blocks.note: late in the evening is close to the night's end

explanation.surface: A kitchen scene where a hair is fished out of a pie baked late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remove hair from pie' looks like one kitchen action; the definition stops at 'hair', and 'from' only joins it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To epilate is the technical verb for taking body hair out by the roots, as with waxing or depilatory devices.

clue.text: Pound returned by fair English fellow

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so these letters run backwards

blocks.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight
fair, as in passable or all right
standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A decent English chap gives back a pound he borrowed.
explanation.walkthrough: Pound here is the weight unit lb, not money; turned round it starts the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloke is informal British slang for a man or guy, an everyday equivalent of fellow.

clue.text: Boy clutching map of North European region

indicators.note: to clutch is to grip tightly, so one piece holds the other inside it

blocks.note: a lad is a boy
a plan is a map or diagram, as of a building or town

explanation.surface: A boy holds tight to a map of somewhere in northern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole phrase after 'map of'; 'map' itself supplies letters, not the sense of a chart for the region.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapland is the Arctic territory of the Sami people spanning northern Norway, Sweden, Finland and part of Russia.

clue.text: Statement about rule applied to eggs

indicators.note: to turn about is to face the other way, so the combined letters run backwards

blocks.note: a law is a rule
placed next to; a positional joiner
ova is the Latin plural for eggs

explanation.surface: A pronouncement on regulations governing eggs, perhaps from a food standards body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning', introducing the topic, but it turns round the whole string of rule plus eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: An avowal is an open declaration or affirmation, so it is a kind of formal statement made publicly.

clue.text: Good artist following through with drug

indicators.note: coming after something places a piece behind it in the line

blocks.note: via means by way of, through
standard abbreviation for good
RA, Royal Academician, is the stock crossword artist

explanation.surface: A fine painter seeing a project through with the help of some medication.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists good-artist first, but 'following' puts those letters after the word for through.
explanation.definitionFit: Viagra is the brand name of sildenafil, a well-known prescription medicine for erectile dysfunction.

clue.text: Octopus originally caught in net close to home left with a sad expression

indicators.note: what something was originally is how it began, so only its opening letter is wanted
something caught in a trap sits inside it, so one piece goes within another
the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is taken

blocks.note: a web is a net or mesh
initial letter
final letter
having left is having gone

explanation.surface: An octopus snared in a fishing net near the shore wears a mournful look as it is carried away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to home' feels like 'near the house', but it just means the end letter of 'home'.
explanation.definitionFit: Woebegone describes someone looking miserable or full of sorrow, so the adjective matches having a sad face.

clue.text: Germanic siren featuring in folklore leitmotif

indicators.note: something featuring in a work appears inside it, so the letters lie within the text that follows

blocks.note: the letters run across the boundary of these two words

explanation.surface: A legendary German temptress who recurs as a theme in folk tales and music.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is almost literally true: the Rhine maiden is a recurring motif in German folklore and song.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is the legendary Rhine maiden whose singing lured sailors onto rocks, a German counterpart of the Greek sirens.

clue.text: Dancing bears seem ill prepared at beginning of scene in musical

indicators.note: dancers move about and change places, so the letters shift position
something prepared has been worked on and put into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
a word's beginning is its opening letter, so only that is taken

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
initial letter

explanation.surface: Performing bears in a stage show look poorly rehearsed at the start of a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Twelve letters from the three words plus the first of 'scene' make the thirteen needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Les Misérables is the long-running stage musical by Boublil and Schönberg, based on Victor Hugo's novel.

clue.text: Cover old swimming pool

blocks.note: a lid is a cover
standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone putting a cover over an aging public swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old swimming pool' looks like one phrase, but 'old' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a lido is a public open-air pool, often an old municipal one from the 1930s.

clue.text: Pad in which Frenchman entertains partner for the evening

indicators.note: a host who entertains takes guests in, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: Pierre is a typical French man's name
a date is someone you go out with for the night

explanation.surface: A flat where a Frenchman brings his evening companion, a hint of romance.
explanation.walkthrough: Pad is the definition, as slang for a flat; 'in which' merely joins it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A pied-à-terre is a small second home kept in a city for occasional stays, and pad is slang for one's flat.

clue.text: Swimming race interrupted by American with recording equipment

indicators.note: swimming things drift and move about, so the letters are moved around
an interruption breaks into the middle of something, so one piece is pushed inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A swimming race broken off by an American carrying recording gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimming race' looks like a gala event, but 'swimming' stirs the letters of the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera is a device for capturing images or video, so it is a standard piece of recording kit.

clue.text: Damage ring at a Spanish resort

blocks.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
to ring, as a bell does; a bell is a ring on the phone
taken as written

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker loses or damages a ring while staying at a Spanish resort.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' that looks like the article before 'Spanish resort' is the answer's final letter; only 'at' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Marbella is a well-known beach town on the Costa del Sol in southern Spain, popular with tourists.

clue.text: Teacher's favourites covering clear iodine with hot piece of lab equipment

indicators.note: a covering goes around what it covers, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: a teacher's pet is a favoured pupil
to clear of something is to rid it
chemical symbol for iodine
standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A chemistry teacher's favourite pupils handling iodine and a hot item in the school lab.
explanation.walkthrough: Teacher's favourites are PETS, which wrap round clear-plus-iodine, then hot follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A Petri dish is the shallow lidded glass or plastic plate that biologists use for culturing bacteria.

clue.text: Doctor and old lady taking part in tiresome process

blocks.note: to doctor results is to rig or falsify them
one's old lady is informal for one's mother
a part in a play is a role

explanation.surface: A GP and an elderly woman both stuck in some tedious procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor is a verb here, meaning tamper with, not a physician; old lady is slang for mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a lengthy, complicated and annoying procedure, so the word captures a tedious bureaucratic palaver.

clue.text: Fictional bear's an adherent of Hindu philosophical system

definitions.text: an adherent of Hindu philosophical system

blocks.note: first meaning: the cartoon bear of Jellystone Park

blocks.clueFragment: an adherent of Hindu philosophical system
blocks.note: second meaning: a practitioner of yoga

explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive but is short for 'is', joining two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hanna-Barbera cartoon character is Yogi Bear, and a person devoted to the discipline of yoga is also called by this name.

clue.text: Soldiers returned with new evidence

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: GIs are American soldiers
standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Troops come back from the field carrying fresh evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: GI is the stock crossword term for an American private soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign is an indication or trace showing something exists, so it serves as evidence of it.

clue.text: Notice allegedly found next to small opening in dense vegetation

indicators.note: what is alleged is only said, so the word is taken for how it is said rather than spelt
an opening is a start, so only the first letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: to notice is to see
wee is Scottish and informal for small
initial letter

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have spotted a little gap in thick undergrowth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dense vegetation' looks like a jungle, but only the first letter of 'dense' is used; vegetation alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaweed is marine algae, plant-like growth found along shores and in the ocean, so it is a kind of vegetation.

clue.text: Unionist line adopted by Arab nation

indicators.note: whoever adopts something takes it in as their own, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula
a range is a line or row, as of mountains

explanation.surface: An Arab state takes up a pro-union political stance.
explanation.walkthrough: An Orangeman is a member of the Orange Order, a Protestant fraternity in Northern Ireland committed to union with Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Orangemen are traditionally staunch supporters of Northern Ireland remaining part of the United Kingdom, hence loyal unionists.

clue.text: Sleepwear's close to neckwear

blocks.note: nigh means near or close
joins the two pieces; next to
a tie is worn round the neck

explanation.surface: Bedclothes are not far off from what you wear round your neck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' looks like the end-letter device, but close is a word meaning near, placed next to the neckwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is the informal name for a nightdress, a loose garment worn to bed, so it counts as sleepwear.

clue.text: It's set in stone to cause trouble

indicators.note: a jewel set in a mount sits within it, so one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: agate is a banded semi-precious stone
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something is fixed in stone, a firm decision meant to stir up a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set in stone' looks like the idiom for unchangeable, but the clue's first word sits inside a gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to stir up unrest or campaign disruptively, so the verb means making trouble.

clue.text: Greedy type welcoming time to prepare snack

indicators.note: a host welcoming guests takes them in, so pieces go inside another

blocks.note: a hog is a greedy person
standard abbreviation for time
to do a meal or a room is to prepare it

explanation.surface: A glutton makes time to whip up something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To prepare' gives DO, as in 'do the vegetables', so 'to' is part of that piece and not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot dog is a sausage served in a split bread roll, a classic quick street food snack.

clue.text: A short stick found during search of burial site

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the last letter is dropped
what happens during something falls within its span, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
a tack is a small nail, from to tack or stick something down; shortened
to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

explanation.surface: Archaeologists find a little stick while searching an ancient burial site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short stick' looks like a twig, but it is a tack missing its final letter, slipped with the article just inside the search word.
explanation.definitionFit: A catacomb is an underground cemetery of tunnels with recesses for tombs, as in Rome or Paris.

clue.text: Animal coming back with tailless bird

indicators.note: something coming back retraces its path, so the letters are read backwards
without a tail means the end is cut off, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a dog is an animal
taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: A creature returns home together with a bird that has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like a joiner, but it is the fodder that loses its last letter; 'tailless' does not apply to the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The godwit is a long-legged wading bird of mudflats with a long, slightly upturned bill.

clue.text: Extremely destructive drug found in storage facility

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: first and last letters
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A dangerous narcotic is discovered in a warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely destructive' reads as 'very harmful', but it takes the outside letters of the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a warehouse or storehouse where goods or vehicles are kept, so it is a place for storage.

clue.text: Temporary transfer for Next employees close to retirement

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is used

blocks.note: the next after first is second
workers, as in management and men
final letter

explanation.surface: Staff at the retailer Next nearing retirement are moved to another post for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: Next is a British high-street clothing chain, hence the capital, but it simply means second.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondment is a temporary posting of an employee to another department or organisation before returning.

clue.text: Spend money to secure Lessing's first dramatic work

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so that alone is taken
to secure is to hold firmly, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: to pay is to spend money
initial letter

explanation.surface: Paying to obtain the rights to Lessing's first drama for staging.
explanation.walkthrough: Lessing could be Doris or the German dramatist Gotthold; either way only the initial matters.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is a piece of drama written for performance on stage, so it is a dramatic work.

clue.text: Doctor given advantage in search for oysters?

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for doctor
an edge is an advantage, as in having the edge

explanation.surface: A physician gets the upper hand while hunting for shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as an example: dredging is used for oysters among other things.
explanation.definitionFit: To dredge is to drag a net or scoop along the seabed, the method used to harvest oysters and scallops.

clue.text: Police officers let suspect get spirit

indicators.note: a suspect account is dubious and not straight, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Detectives allow a suspect to have a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' looks like a noun, the person under arrest, and 'spirit' like alcohol; the Met is London's police force.
explanation.definitionFit: Mettle means courage and strength of character, as in proving one's mettle, a sense shared with spirit.
